notes: rounds/results.py result() does every check in one transaction (POST holds the round lock): non-Open round, superseded build, the tester's own result, a POST to a submitted result, and no form on GET for a submitted result; services.save_result fetches the row by tester and raises ResultSubmitted for a submitted one. M1 drops the tester filter in both reads; M4 removes the POST refusal, the GET read-only branch and the service check, so the form is shown (status still Submitted) and a save turns the result back into a draft. ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); ObservationField(max_length=2000) limits it, so M5's message also says 2001. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_results to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
